title: Apparel body functional execution controls
isolation: Provide only the selected task input directory to the candidate. Never expose fixtures/oracle or other task directories as task input. Oracle files contain target parameters and independent fixture smoke evidence, not public instructions.

tasks.suggested_task_prompt: Fit the existing synthetic neutral body proxy to target-front-mask.png and target-side-mask.png using generator.py and initial-params.json. Execute a constrained parameter fit with the frozen camera and 170 cm height prior. Export fitted params, actual OBJ, front/side/back previews, initial/final per-view silhouette metrics and a short evidence/uncertainty report. Use only the two masks as target evidence; do not invent observed side/back photographs or anatomical truth.

Repair the offline body viewer so its initial actual mesh agrees with the version 2 final body.json and body.obj, including when stale version 1 localStorage already exists. Make height/chest/waist/hip sliders deform actual mesh vertices and keep camera buttons and rotation functional. Execute it in Chromium, exercise stale-cache migration and slider interaction followed by reload, and provide before/after visible browser evidence. Explain the synchronization change and assumptions.
dependencies: Chromium; optional python -m http.server for browser policy

tasks.suggested_task_prompt: Audit measurements.json and depth-claim.png using source-evidence.json, sections.json and actual body.obj. Execute mesh-plane section measurements and choose the central torso contour where disconnected arm loops also intersect. Save corrected measurements with explicit units, scale assumption, evidence status and uncertainty; preserve unavailable bust-point distance as unknown. Correct the misleading depth caption and provide rendered section evidence. Do not claim real-person dimensions from these synthetic controls.
tasks.suggested_start_command: Read README.md and source-evidence.json; load body.obj for section computation
